meta.note: Starting values. Crop coefficients (Kc: initial, mid-season, end) follow FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Table 12, or the closest crop in that table (quinoa: Garcia et al. 2003; Andean tubers: potato values; locoto: pepper values). Cycle length, frost damage temperature and soil pH range are general reference values of the kind listed in FAO ECOCROP and Andean agronomy guides. The data role must check every value against FAO-56, FAO ECOCROP and INIAF before the results are shown as validated.
meta.stage_fractions_note: Generic split of the cycle into the four FAO-56 growth stages; FAO-56 Table 11 gives crop- and region-specific lengths.
meta.main_crop_note: Only crops of 90 days or more (plus perennials and fallow) fill a year of the three-year rotation; shorter vegetables are shown in the catalogue as crops to fit between main crops.
meta.groups_note: Groups tree (fruit trees and shrubs), herb (aromatic plants) and flower are shown in the catalogue but not used in three-year rotations.
meta.min_mean_temp_note: min_mean_temp_c: warm-season crops need at least this mean temperature during the cycle (ECOCROP optimal range); below it the engine lowers the climate score.
meta.local_note: local: false marks crops that are rare in the Cochabamba valleys; they enter rotations only when the farmer prefers or already sows them.
